To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of neurotrophic factors on cell phenotype vary between cell types and between cells of the same type.
neurotrophin regulation varies with cell type and with cell-to-cell variability.
neurotrophin regulation depends on cell context and that this can occur even between individual cells of a clonal relation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how neurotrophin signaling pathways regulate cell phenotype.
the mechanisms of action of neurotrophin signaling in the regulation of electrical and morphological differentiation.
the regulation of neuronal phenotype and function by the neurotrophins and the Trk receptors they activate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Trk receptor activation does not have a defined set and obligatory effects on neuronal phenotype, but instead can have a variety of effects on different cell types and even within individual cell types.
neurotrophins regulate cell phenotype in a cell context dependent manner.
neurotrophins can regulate ionic currents and morphological differentiation depending on the cell types and cell contexts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
neurotrophin signaling is a complex process that is influenced not only by the nature of the ligand, but also by the nature of target cells.

Trk receptors are not only capable of regulating multiple target genes, but that they are also capable of regulating different subsets of target genes in different cell types, or even in different cells of a single cell type.
Trk receptors are necessary for neurotrophins to induce neurite extension in PC12 cells, but they are not sufficient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

neurotrophins are not simply a set of "neuronal" growth factors, but rather are a class of signaling molecules that can have different effects on neuronal phenotype depending on the cell in which they act.

Trk receptors can be considered as molecular switches that can be activated by neurotrophin ligands, but the resulting phenotypic outcomes are dependent on the cellular context in which the Trk receptors are expressed.
the regulatory effects of Trk receptors on cell phenotype are context-dependent.
